_comment: Produced by: python scripts/price_check.py week-14-postgres-no-passwords
Written before deployment. Committed so the charges this week accepted are public.
THIS IS THE FIRST WEEK SINCE 11 WITH REAL PER-HOUR COMPUTE, and the first
where the headline feature is the expensive one. High availability is not a
checkbox: the Burstable tier does not support HA at all, so HA forces
General Purpose, and HA then doubles that compute.
CORRECTED 2026-11-22: an earlier version of this file claimed a $1,883/hour
meter. That was a 3-year reservation term total misread as an hourly rate by
price_check.py. The number was questioned and did not survive the check.
REWRITTEN 2026-11-22 after the design settled. The server is no longer the
only billable thing: proving a PRIVATE database needs a client inside the
network, and proving failover downtime needs that client writing across the
failover. So this week also runs one small VM, one private endpoint and one
private DNS zone. Two of those three were invisible to the gate until today.
AMENDED 2026-11-22, same session: a NAT gateway was added to the design.
Default outbound access is an implicit platform behaviour Microsoft advises against relying on; the portal already creates private subnets and new API versions after
31 March 2026 set defaultOutboundAccess=false. Built explicitly so the client can
install a PostgreSQL client. The egress path is now deliberate -- which is
what a platform team has to do anyway -- and it is the only public IP in the
week. Nothing accepts an inbound connection from the internet.

acknowledged.vCore: NOT REACHED. 32 tiers, dearest 76.979/hr -- a ~96-vCore Memory Optimized server, about $1,847/day. Real and reachable if the wrong SKU is picked, which is why the sku_name is pinned in Terraform AND the guardrail at mg-katta denies any PostgreSQL SKU outside a 2-vCore allowlist. CORRECTED 2026-11-22: this previously read 1,883.00/hr. That figure was a THREE-YEAR RESERVATION TOTAL that price_check.py was reading as an hourly rate -- the same SKU's consumption rate is 0.1791/hr. The tool now excludes type=Reservation rows; 28 were being counted here.
acknowledged.1 vCore: NOT REACHED. 14 tiers up to 0.23814/hr -- per-vCore rates for SKU generations this week does not use. The chosen generation is pinned.
acknowledged.2 vCore: THE ONE THIS WEEK USES, at the General Purpose rate of 0.1026/hr per vCore = 0.2052/hr, doubled to 0.4104/hr by HA. Acknowledged because it is deliberate, bounded by a 3-hour window, and is the point of the week.
acknowledged.B1MS: NOT USED. 0.0204/hr, the cheapest compute available and rejected on purpose: the Burstable tier supports no form of high availability, so it cannot carry this week's claim.
acknowledged.B2ms vCore: NOT USED. Burstable family, no HA support.
acknowledged.B4ms vCore: NOT USED. Burstable family, no HA support.
acknowledged.B8ms vCore: NOT USED. Burstable family, no HA support.
acknowledged.B12ms vCore: NOT USED. Burstable family, no HA support.
acknowledged.B16ms vCore: NOT USED. Burstable family, no HA support.
acknowledged.B20ms vCore: NOT USED. 1.63200/hr. Burstable family, no HA support.
acknowledged.Extended Support vCore: NOT USED. 0.084/hr, charged for running a PostgreSQL major version past its community end-of-life. This week deploys a currently supported major version.
acknowledged.Auto Tune vCore: NOT USED. The Autonomous Database Tuning Service is not enabled.
acknowledged.Ultra Disk Throughput Prov Throughput (M: NOT USED. Server storage is left at the default managed-disk tier; no Ultra Disk is provisioned.
acknowledged.Premium SSDv2 Throughput Prov Throughput: NOT USED. Premium SSD v2 is an opt-in storage type this week does not select.
acknowledged.IOPS Scaling Provisioned IOPS: NOT USED. IOPS scaling is not enabled; storage stays at the provisioned default.
acknowledged.Standard Private Endpoint: USED, one of them, at 0.01/hr. Priced under armRegionName 'Global', which is why the gate never showed it before 2026-11-22 -- a region-only filter returned nothing for it. This is how the database is reached with no public endpoint at all.
acknowledged.Fixed Private Endpoint T1: NOT USED. 14.00/hr, about $336/day, for a fixed-capacity Private Link endpoint. The week creates a standard private endpoint; nothing in the Terraform can select this tier.
acknowledged.Private Zone: USED, one zone, at 0.50 per zone per month -- about $0.0007 for a 3-hour window. Billed on unitOfMeasure '1', which the gate classed as a USAGE meter until 2026-11-22; a flat monthly charge was sitting in the usage list where nobody has to acknowledge it.
acknowledged.Public Zone: NOT USED. 0.50 per zone/month for public DNS. The week's zone is private; there is no public record anywhere in it.
acknowledged.Private Resolver Inbound Endpoint: NOT USED. 180.00 per month, and the single most expensive thing this week could accidentally create. A DNS Private Resolver is only needed to resolve the private zone from OUTSIDE Azure; the client here is a VM inside the same virtual network, which resolves through Azure-provided DNS for free.
acknowledged.Private Resolver Outbound Endpoint: NOT USED. 180.00 per month. Same product, other direction.
acknowledged.Private Resolver DNS Forwarding Ruleset: NOT USED. 2.50 per month, and it cannot exist without a resolver this week does not create.
acknowledged.Standard Service Endpoint Virtual Networ: NOT USED. 0.10/hr for a Private Link SERVICE -- publishing your own service behind Private Link. This week consumes Microsoft's, which is the private endpoint meter above.
acknowledged.Standard Subscription: NOT USED. 0.10/hr for Azure Virtual Network Manager, per subscription enrolled. No network manager is created.
acknowledged.Standard Virtual Network: NOT USED. 0.02/hr, also Virtual Network Manager, per managed VNet. Same reason. A plain virtual network is free.
acknowledged.Managed IP Management: NOT USED. 0.00027/hr, Virtual Network Manager again.
acknowledged.Standard Appliance Standard Unit: NOT USED. 3.375/hr for a Virtual Network Routing Appliance. The week creates no appliance and no route table.
acknowledged.Basic Appliance Unit: NOT USED. 0.675/hr. Same product, lower tier.
acknowledged.A8 Management NIC: NOT USED. 2.50/hr, an Accelerated Connections management NIC. Not an option on the VM size this week pins.
acknowledged.TAP: NOT USED. 0.015/hr for a virtual network TAP. No traffic mirroring is configured.
acknowledged.Standard IPv4 Static Public IP: USED, exactly ONE, at 0.005/hr, and it belongs to the NAT gateway rather than to anything that listens. Outbound only: the database has public network access disabled, and the VM is reached through the Azure control plane with az vm run-command rather than SSH. There is no inbound public endpoint in this week.
acknowledged.Standard Static IP Addresses: NOT USED. 0.006/hr, a public IP PREFIX. Same reason.
acknowledged.Global Static Public IP: NOT USED. 0.012/hr, a global public IP prefix.
acknowledged.Global IPv4 Static Public IP: NOT USED. 0.01/hr, a global-tier public IP.
acknowledged.Basic IPv4 Static Public IP: NOT USED. 0.0036/hr. The Basic public IP SKU is retired for new addresses and the week creates none anyway.
acknowledged.Reachability Analysis Diagnostic Tool AP: NOT USED. 0.10 per analysis run, an on-demand Virtual Network Manager diagnostic. Billed on a bare '1' unit, so it is listed as flat; it is per-invocation and nothing in this week invokes it. Connectivity here is proved by connecting, not by asking Azure whether it would work.
acknowledged.Standard Gateway: USED, one of them, at 0.045/hr. The week's explicit egress path: the client VM has no public IP, and default outbound access is an implicit platform behaviour Microsoft recommends against relying on -- the portal already creates private subnets, and for API versions after 31 March 2026 new virtual networks set defaultOutboundAccess = false. Priced under armRegionName 'Global', so it was invisible to the gate before the region filter was widened today.
acknowledged.StandardV2 Log Enabled: NOT USED. 4.00/month for NAT gateway v2 flow logging. The week creates a Standard gateway and enables no logging on it.

NOT REACHED, all of it. Azure prices every VM size as its own flat hourly meter, so this one service contributes thousands of families and a ceiling of 533.70/hr (an 896-vCPU M-series). TWO mechanisms keep the week away from it, and neither is an intention: the size is pinned to Standard_D2als_v7 in the Terraform, and the deny policy assigned at mg-katta refuses any size outside a 1-2 vCPU allowlist two scopes above this subscription -- proved 2026-11-22 with RequestDisallowedByPolicy on a deliberate attempt. The week's own VM bills 0.0962/hr, measured in week 11.
NOT REACHED beyond one managed disk. Same shape as Virtual Machines: every disk size and redundancy combination is its own flat monthly meter, ceiling 4,915.20/month for a P80 ZRS disk. The week creates exactly one disk -- the VM's OS disk, pinned in Terraform to StandardSSD_LRS at 30 GB, about 2.40/month prorated to pennies -- and no storage account of any kind. The database's own storage bills under Azure Database for PostgreSQL, not here.

the_tier_decision.burstable_b1ms: 0.0204/hr. Cheapest, and REJECTED -- MEASURED 2026-11-22, not quoted: `az postgres flexible-server create --tier Burstable --sku-name Standard_B1ms --high-availability SameZone` is refused with 'High availability is not supported for the Burstable tier.' Worth testing because the docs only rule out the ZONE-REDUNDANT case on Burstable, and the capability API lists both HA modes against every Burstable SKU -- the same API that claimed zone-redundant was available in a region that then refused it.
the_tier_decision.general_purpose_2_vcore_with_ha: 0.4104/hr -- HA doubles compute because it runs a standby. CHOSEN. Zone-redundant and same-zone cost the same, so the open question about which mode this region grants is not a cost question.
the_tier_decision.why: A configured HA setting proves nothing. The week's claim is a failover actually performed with the downtime measured, and that is only possible on a tier that supports HA.

predicted_cost._comment: Stated BEFORE deployment so the invoice can contradict it.
predicted_cost.bound: a TIME window, not a daily cap -- these meters bill per hour and cannot be capped like ingestion
predicted_cost.predicted_total_usd: under 2.50, allowing for the deploy taking longer than planned
predicted_cost.discipline: deploy, validate, fail over, measure, destroy in one sitting. There is no cap that saves this one; only teardown does.
predicted_cost.data_processed: NAT gateway also bills 0.045/GB. Installing psql moves tens of megabytes, so under a cent; stated because it is a usage meter the gate does not demand an acknowledgement for.

residual_risks: A per-hour meter has no equivalent of week 13's daily_quota_gb. The only bound is destroying it, so cleanup.sh runs the same day and the figure plan has no slot that requires the server to survive overnight.
A failed teardown here costs ~$13/day rather than ~$0, so cleanup verification asserts the server, the VM and the private endpoint are gone against Azure rather than trusting the destroy exit code.
Storage is billed from creation to deletion and is not prorated by usage, so an idle server still charges for its disk -- and with HA it charges for the standby's disk too.
HA doubles compute whichever mode this region grants. If zone-redundant is refused and the week falls back to same-zone, the cost is identical and only the resilience claim changes.

The gate found two of its own blind spots on this week -- meters priced under region 'Global' and meters priced on a bare '1' unit. Both are closed. Anything priced in a way neither the region filter nor the unit list anticipates is still invisible, which is why the published figure comes from the invoice.

measured_cost._comment: Read from Cost Management 2026-11-23, the day after teardown. The prediction above was written before deploying so this could contradict it.
measured_cost.vs_prediction: predicted 1.74 for 3 hours, about 0.73 for the 1h15m actually run; measured 0.6478, roughly 11% under
measured_cost.note: Virtual Network and Azure DNS are the private endpoint and the private zone -- the two meters this gate was blind to until 2026-11-22. They billed.
